method: Miha taught us a great deal of theory and asked about our intended final outputs as well as our undergraduate majors. I shared my idea for a spatial installation designed to help people—who use ACG culture to escape reality and retreat into their comfort zones—overcome psychological challenges in their real lives. Since I mentioned wanting to leverage AI to assist them, MiHA encouraged me to read extensively on the subject, though I might still alter my final project. She also introduced us to the mindset of an artist and showcased numerous artworks, all of which I found incredibly enlightening.
related_work:
MIHA Board – A template designed for accessible riding.
TikTok Video – There is no standard answer in art; it is harder than math.
conclusion_future_work: Miha is truly a highly professional art teacher; she shared insights from her graduate studies, and I really admired her distinctive style—it immediately commanded the kind of respect one naturally feels for an artist. She introduced the reading for the coming week, "Criptech and the Art of Access." Although English is not my native language, the article provided a detailed explanation of the deeper meaning behind the term "crip" (highlighting just how vast the nuances of the language can be). It also raised some questions for me: when it comes to initiatives where art and technology combine to benefit humanity, people often instinctively focus solely on the technology while overlooking the artistic element. How can I better highlight the artistic dimension so that the work is immediately recognized as a fusion of art and technology? I hope to find the answer to this in the future.
results_discussion: Finally, Miha asked us to write a statement outlining our accessibility needs and provided several templates for reference. Honestly, I had never written anything like this before, nor had I ever encountered a school that placed such emphasis on students' mental well-being—though perhaps the small size of our program plays a role in that. I truly appreciated the opportunity, so I wrote a detailed account covering my needs, expectations, and ideas that I felt would be immensely beneficial to my studies and artistic practice. Naturally, I kept my requests reasonable; I certainly wouldn't ask for anything unreasonable. I look forward to a friendly, comfortable atmosphere for communication and learning in the future.
title: The First Week of Getting to Know MIHA
introduction: It was a disaster—while cooking on Thursday morning, I accidentally set off the smoke alarm and had no idea what to do. Firefighters ended up knocking on my door, and I had to explain the situation to them; consequently, I was late for Miha’s class. It was so embarrassing, but Miha didn't blame us. She even had me reintroduce myself and didn't mark me as late. She also taught me a lot of theory and shared case studies regarding creative technology, asked about my interests, and offered some general guidance on my direction.
